answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Each submission hangs on the tide of a task receipt, and the river is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. The lotus of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
